about.title: About HEX to HSL Converter - HSL Color Space
about.description: The HEX to HSL Converter transforms hexadecimal color codes into HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) values and vice versa. HSL separates hue from saturation and lightness, which can make color adjustments easier to review. The HSL color model is useful for creating color variations, adjusting brightness, and building color schemes in design and web development projects.

faq.q: What does HSL stand for and how does it work?
faq.a: HSL stands for Hue, Saturation, and Lightness. Hue represents the color type (0-360°), Saturation controls color intensity (0-100%), and Lightness adjusts brightness (0-100%). This model is more intuitive than RGB for color manipulation.

faq.q: Why use HSL instead of HEX or RGB?
faq.a: HSL is more intuitive for color adjustments. You can easily modify brightness (lightness) or color intensity (saturation) without affecting the base color (hue). This makes it ideal for creating color variations and harmonious palettes.

faq.q: What are the HSL value ranges?
faq.a: Hue ranges from 0-360 degrees representing position on the color wheel, Saturation from 0-100% controlling color intensity (0% = grayscale, 100% = full color), and Lightness from 0-100% controlling brightness (0% = black, 50% = normal, 100% = white).

faq.q: Can I use HSL values directly in CSS?
faq.a: Yes! Modern browsers fully support HSL values in CSS. Use hsl(hue, saturation%, lightness%) syntax or hsla(hue, saturation%, lightness%, alpha) for colors with transparency. HSL is often preferred for CSS custom properties and color manipulation.
